Figure 2: Example from the MATH subset of ProcessBench. We report scores from two PRMs based on Llama + PRM800k. The PDDL-trained PRM more strongly penalizes the incorrect combinatorial formulation, where the reasoning restricts the solution space to permutations of fixed groups, excluding valid interleavings across types.

Figure 3: Example from the Medicine subset of MR-Ben. We report scores from two PRMs based on Qwen2.5Math-PRM-7B. The PDDL-trained PRM assigns a lower score to the fourth reasoning step, correctly penalizing a biologically incorrect justification that conflates RNA composition with its functional role in protein synthesis.
